title: FlowPrefill: Decoupling Preemption from Prefill Scheduling Granularity to Mitigate Head-of-Line Blocking in LLM Serving
technique: operator-level prefill preemption + event-driven slack-aware EDF scheduling and SLO-aware batching to avoid head-of-line blocking

optimized_metrics.evidence: we propose FlowPrefill, a TTFT-goodput-optimized serving system
Since FlowPrefill performs preemption only during the prefill phase, we focus on TTFT SLO attainment as the primary metric.
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: we focus on TTFT SLO attainment as the primary metric

optimized_metrics.evidence: heterogeneous latency requirements. To maximize goodput, we adopt an SLO-aware batching strategy

headline_claim.text: Evaluation on real-world production traces shows that FlowPrefill improves maximum goodput by up to 5.6x compared to state-of-the-art systems while satisfying heterogeneous SLOs.

reported_metrics.where: Figs 9-14 (vs request rate and SLO scale)
Figs 11, 14 (throughput under batch token budgets / single-SLO)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: goodput, defined as the maximum sustainable request rate under an SLO attainment goal (e.g., 90%)
metric_definitions.notes: request-rate based goodput; evaluation: 'We define goodput as the maximum sustainable request rate at 90% SLO attainment.' (§6.1). TTFT SLO only; decode latency not an SLO

metric_definitions.definition_quote: we focus on TTFT SLO attainment as the primary metric
metric_definitions.notes: attainment fraction of requests meeting per-task TTFT SLO

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We define the preemption blocking time as the interval between the moment a higher-priority request sends a preemption signal and the moment the new request can be submitted (i.e., when the ACK is received in Figure 7).
slack = deadline - current_time - predicted TTFT ... The deadline is the request arrival time plus its TTFT SLO
metric_definitions.notes: TTFT is measured from arrival, i.e. includes queueing; predicted by offline fitted model

slo_spec: Per-task TTFT SLOs (Table 2), e.g. Llama3-8B text 0.25s, image 0.5s, search 4.0s, file 6.0s; Qwen2.5-14B 0.4/0.8/6.5/9.0s; Llama3-70B 1.0/2.0/15.0/18.0s; assigned from prior work and application semantics; SLO scale parameter linearly scales them; goodput at 90% attainment
load_regime: trace replay with request-rate scale and SLO-scale sweeps (QwenTrace)
tradeoff_acknowledged: chunk size: smaller improves responsiveness but degrades computational efficiency/throughput; larger maximizes throughput but exacerbates blocking (motivation). FlowPrefill matches baseline throughput in single-SLO workload (Fig 14).
hardware: 8x NVIDIA A800-SXM4-80GB (NVLink 200GB/s); motivation experiments on A100-40GB
workloads: QwenTrace production trace (text, image, search, file task types), single-turn, random tokens of matching lengths
extractor_notes: Optimization is prefill/TTFT only; TPOT/decode latency not optimized or constrained. Two-column PDF; read via pdftotext (non-layout). Percentile of TTFT not used; attainment-based.
load_class_quote: SLO-scale and request-rate sweeps over trace replay (QwenTrace): 'trace replay with request-rate scale and SLO-scale sweeps' (§6.1)
repass_log: GOODPUT, TTFT(SLO), SLO_ATT all kept as design (system goal / SLO / batching to maximize goodput)
